CHROMIUM: Use estimated throughput to avoid signal based roaming decision Previously, the estimated throughput was used to enable roaming to a better AP. However, this information was not used when considering a roam to an AP that has better signal strength, but smaller estimated throughput. This could result in allowing roaming from 5 GHz band to 2.4 GHz band in cases where 2.4 GHz band has significantly higher signal strength, but still a lower throughput estimate. Make this less likely to happen by increasing/reducing the minimum required signal strength difference based on the estimated throughputs of the current and selected AP. In addition, add more details about the selection process to the debug log to make it easier to determine whaty happened and why. Cherry-picked commit did not apply cleanly due to log level conflict. Using CHROMIUM tag instead of UPSTREAM tag. Signed-off-by: Jouni Malinen <j@w1.fi> (cherry picked from commit 8d1e693186336f85bf5d86bd094b5c9bd6f8fd02) Change-Id: Iaa42f9eafdb6e9b51114199535a671a1b4e20ad7 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1008996 Commit-Ready: Matthew Wang <matthewmwang@chromium.org> Tested-by: Matthew Wang <matthewmwang@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Matthew Wang <matthewmwang@chromium.org>

debugd: log_tool: add threads information Showing the pid and ppid for relationship of threads and processes. Showing current cpu percent, nice value, thread stat, thread total cpu time is also useful. "threads": ps -T axo pid,ppid,spid,pcpu,ni,stat,time,comm "ps": ps aux, is roughly equivalent to "ps axo user,pid,pcpu,pmem,vsz,rss,tty,stat,start,time,args" The fields: pid: process id ppid: parent pid spid: thread id pcpu: cpu usage in percent pmem: rss in percent vsz: virtual memory size in KiB rss: resident set size in KiB tty: controlling tty stat: process or thread stat start: process or thread start time time: cumulative process or thread CPU time comm: executable name or thread name args: command with all its arguments note that comm and args have the same header name: COMMAND. "threads" and "ps" are separated because some fields are suitable to display for each thread, and some fields are suitable to display for each process. If "ps" and "threads" are combined, there are some duplicated data and it's harder to read. "threads": $ ps -T axo pid,ppid,spid,pcpu,ni,stat,time,comm | wc -c 18244 "ps": $ ps aux | wc -c 31794 "combined": $ ps -T axo pid,ppid,spid,pcpu,ni,stat,time,comm,user,pmem,vsz,rss,\ > tty,start,args | wc -c 138109 BUG=chromium:830589 TEST=Run from command line: dbus-send --type=method_call --system \ --print-reply --dest=org.chromium.debugd /org/chromium/debugd \ org.chromium.debugd.GetLog string:threads Change-Id: I03c3e4131249fe0a06b3bd0a66acf4911813ea39 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1084355 Commit-Ready: Vovo Yang <vovoy@chromium.org> Tested-by: Vovo Yang <vovoy@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: ALSA: core: Assure control device to be registered at last The commit 289ca025ee1d ("ALSA: Use priority list for managing device list") changed the way to register/disconnect/free devices via a single priority list. This helped to make behavior consistent, but it also changed a slight behavior change: namely, the control device is registered earlier than others, while it was supposed to be the very last one. I've put SNDRV_DEV_CONTROL in the current position as the release of ctl elements often conflict with the private ctl elements some PCM or other components may create, which often leads to a double-free. But, the order of register and disconnect should be indeed fixed as expected in the early days: the control device gets registered at last, and disconnected at first. This patch changes the priority list order to move SNDRV_DEV_CONTROL as the last guy to assure the register / disconnect order. Meanwhile, for keeping the messy resource release order, manually treat the control and lowlevel devices as last freed one. Additional note: The lowlevel device is the device where a card driver creates at probe. And, we still keep the release order control -> lowlevel, as there might be link from a control element back to a lowlevel object.
